item.title: Generic cyclotomic type-A support is bounded by rank
item.statement:
Let $k$ have characteristic zero, let $\xi\in k^\times$ have infinite
multiplicative order, and fix a finite integral multicharge
$m_1,\ldots,m_\ell$. Write $S=\{m_j:1\le j\le\ell\}$.
Use the arbitrary-base presentations of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]] to define
$H_d^{\deg}$ by $\prod_j(x_1-m_j)=0$ and $H_d^{\xi}$ by
$\prod_j(X_1-\xi^{m_j})=0$.
For $d>0$, every nonzero joint generalized weight in the regular module has
labels $\nu\in\mathbb Z^d$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ respectively
$\xi^{\nu_r}$, and
$$\min_{s\in S}|\nu_r-s|\le d-1.$$
Thus both algebras have finite joint spectral decompositions defined over $k$.

Use the directed line $i\to i+1$ on $\mathbb Z$, with $d_i=1$,
$Q_{i,i+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $Q_{i+1,i}(u,v)=u-v$ and $Q_{ij}=1$ for
$|i-j|>1$. Define the rank-$d$ cyclotomic KLR algebra as the direct sum of its
finite-content presentations, with first-strand exponents
$\lambda_i=\#\{j:m_j=i\}$. Every nonzero word idempotent satisfies the same
bound, so this rank algebra is a finite sum of finite-dimensional graded
content algebras. Any interval containing
$[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]$ gives exactly the same rank-$d$ algebra;
enlarging it introduces only zero word idempotents. Rank zero is $k$.
At level zero every positive rank is zero. This lemma supplies support and
finite windows; it asserts no Hecke--KLR isomorphism or basis correspondence.
item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The presentations and parameters of the Statement.

[F1] The arbitrary monic cyclotomic Hecke quotients are finite-dimensional by
[[lem-cyclotomic-hecke-bounded-ordered-monomials-span]]. Their mixed and
quadratic relations are those of
[[def-type-a-affine-presentations-and-charged-cyclotomic-quotients]].

[F2] In the KLR presentation, a crossing between distant colors has square
$1$ and interchanges their word idempotents
([[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]]).
On any finite color interval, homogeneous cyclotomic content algebras are
finite-dimensional with nilpotent dots
([[lem-cyclotomic-klr-dot-annihilators-and-finite-root-strings]]).

## Proof

1.1 Work over a finite splitting extension for the finitely many minimal polynomials of the commuting polynomial generators in the finite regular module of [F1]. Simultaneous primary decomposition gives joint generalized eigenspaces. On such a weight, the first value is a charge root, because the first cyclotomic polynomial annihilates the module. In the degenerate case connect distinct values differing by $1$; in the nondegenerate case connect distinct nonzero values whose ratio is $\xi$ or $\xi^{-1}$. This defines a graph on the distinct values in each word, with at most $d$ vertices. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 For a KLR word, form the induced line graph on its distinct colors. If a component contains no charge, move its first occurrence left across all earlier letters. These letters lie in other components, so their color differences exceed $1$; [F2] makes every crossing invertible. The resulting word idempotent is nonzero if the original was, but its first color has exponent zero, so the cyclotomic relation kills it. This contradiction shows that each component contains a charge. A component with at most $d$ vertices is an interval, and every color has distance at most $d-1$ from a charge in that component. [F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The mixed relations give intertwiners $\theta_r=s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})+1$ and $\Theta_r=T_r(1-X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})+1-\xi$. Direct multiplication gives $\theta_r^2=1-(x_r-x_{r+1})^2$ and $\Theta_r^2=(1-\xi X_{r+1}X_r^{-1})(1-\xi X_rX_{r+1}^{-1})$; they interchange the two polynomial generators and commute with the others. For example $s_r(x_r-x_{r+1})=-(x_r-x_{r+1})s_r-2$, which yields the first square identity; the second follows by inserting $T_r^2=(\xi-1)T_r+\xi$ and $T_rX_rT_r=\xi X_{r+1}$. Between values in different graph components these squares have nonzero constant terms, hence are invertible on the generalized weight space. Each intertwiner therefore gives an isomorphism onto the swapped generalized weight space. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Suppose a component contains no charge root. Its earliest occurrence in the word can be moved to the first position by the invertible swaps of step 2.1: every preceding value belongs to a different component. The resulting nonzero weight space has an uncharged first value, contradicting the first cyclotomic relation. Consequently each component contains a charge root. A simple path from that root to any vertex has length at most $d-1$, so the value is an integer within $d-1$ of an integral charge, respectively a power $\xi^a$ with $|a-m_j|\le d-1$. Infinite order of $\xi$ makes the integer labels unique. All spectral values therefore belong to $k$, and their polynomial primary projectors descend to $k$ by the Chinese remainder identity. [step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Only finitely many words satisfy this bound. In every content presentation the generators and relations use only colors already present in that content, so replacing the full line by a finite interval containing the bound changes none of these presentations. All omitted contents have zero word idempotents by step 1.2. On the finite interval [F2] supplies finite-dimensionality and nilpotent dots, and the finite sum is finite-dimensional. This identifies the full rank algebra with each sufficiently large finite window, including compatibility of larger windows on the same generators. At level zero the first exponent is always zero, killing every positive-rank word; the Hecke polynomial is $1$ and gives the same zero quotient. Rank zero is the ground field by definition. No basis correspondence or Hecke--KLR inverse map has been used. [step 3.1, step 1.2, F1, F2, given] ∎

item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The characteristic-zero field, finite integer interval, multiset, presentations, completions and specified series in the Statement.

[F1] The native KLR presentation in [[def-quiver-hecke-klr-algebra-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]] has the two equal-color dot moves for $\tau$, the quadratic polynomial $Q$, and the reversed-word braid numerator $[Q(u,v)-Q(w,v)]/(w-u)$. Replacing $\tau$ by $-\psi$ gives $\psi u-v\psi=-1$, $\psi v-u\psi=1$, and $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2=[Q(u,v)-Q(w,v)]/(w-u)$ on colors $(a,b,a)$.

[F2] The degenerate affine Hecke generator presentation of [[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]] over $\mathbb C$ has the relations listed in the Statement; here that presentation defines the algebra over $k$, and its basis and faithful action are proved below. The generators $s_r$ permute positions; the distinct notation $\sigma_r$ below means actual permutation operators on polynomial or formal coefficient functions.

## Proof

**Given:** The data and conventions of the Statement, and [F1]–[F2].

1.1 The coefficient completions. A symmetric polynomial in the commuting $x$ is central: the mixed relation gives $s_rf=(\sigma_rf)s_r-(f-\sigma_rf)/(x_r-x_{r+1})$, first on monomials by induction, then on polynomials. A symmetric $f$ has zero correction. The fiber of the elementary symmetric polynomials over their values on $\beta$ consists exactly of the ordered permutations of $\beta$: the coordinates are roots with multiplicities of $\prod_{a\in\beta}(t-a)$. Its radical is the intersection of the finitely many corresponding maximal ideals, by the polynomial factorization and the fact that every coordinate satisfies this monic polynomial. The elementary-symmetric ideal and this radical have cofinal powers, since the fiber is finite dimensional and its radical nilpotent. Chinese remainders and completion therefore give $\mathcal B_\beta$ with local coordinates $x_r-\nu_r$. On the KLR side symmetric dot polynomials are central by [F1], and the same argument at the all-zero fiber shows that its coefficient completion is $\mathcal B_\beta$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Invertible tables. If $a\ne b$ the integer $a-b$ is a nonzero unit in $k$, so $z^{-1}$ exists as a formal geometric series. In the backward case $a=b+1$, $q=z^{-1}$ has constant $1$. In the other unequal cases $q=1-z^{-1}$ has constant $1-(a-b)^{-1}$, which could vanish only when $a-b=1$, already excluded. Equal colors give constant $1$. For unequal colors $p_{ba}(v,u)=-p_{ab}(u,v)$. Direct multiplication gives $q_{ab}(u,v)q_{ba}(v,u)=1-z^{-2}$ on nonadjacent colors; on a forward arrow it gives $-(z-1)/z^2=(1-z^{-2})/(v-u)$ since $z=-1+u-v$; on a backward arrow it gives $(z+1)/z^2=(1-z^{-2})/(u-v)$ since $z=1+u-v$. Thus $Q_{ab}q_{ab}\sigma(q_{ba})=1-p_{ab}^2$ in all unequal cases, with no division by a nonunit left unresolved. [step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 A concrete KLR action. On $\mathcal B_\beta$, dots multiply and idempotents project. Define $E_r=(\sigma_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$ on equal adjacent colors. The numerator is divisible by the denominator for polynomials and formal series, so $E_r$ preserves the coefficient algebra. For unequal source colors $(a,b)$ define $\psi_r(fe(\nu))=c_{ab}(y_r,y_{r+1})\sigma_r(f)e(s_r\nu)$, where $c_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $c_{ab}(u,v)=1$ otherwise. These explicit operators prove the local relations in the following five cases. [step 2.1, given, construct, algebra]

4.1 Quadratic and dot moves. Write $\delta=u-v$. On equal colors $E^2=0$, since $E(f)$ is invariant under $\sigma$, and $Eu-vE=-1$, $Ev-uE=1$ follow by expanding the numerator. On unequal colors the dot moves are permutation identities and $\psi^2=c_{ba}(u,v)c_{ab}(v,u)=Q_{ab}(u,v)$. Indeed these products are $v-u$ on a forward arrow, $u-v$ on a backward arrow, and $1$ off edges. Disjoint crossings commute because their variables and their two-color factors are disjoint. Idempotent moves and commutative dot relations hold by construction. [F1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Three distinct colors. Put $u=y_1,v=y_2,w=y_3$, $s=\sigma_1,t=\sigma_2$, $\rho=sts=tst$, $L=\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1$, $M=\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$. On a source $(a,b,c)$ with all colors distinct, direct consecutive application of step 3.1 gives both $L(f)$ and $M(f)$ equal to $c_{bc}(u,v)c_{ac}(u,w)c_{ab}(v,w)\rho(f)$ in the $(c,b,a)$ summand. The three pair factors commute. Hence $L=M$ for every edge pattern among three distinct integer colors. [step 4.1, step 3.1, algebra]

6.1 Exactly the first two equal. On $(a,a,b)$, $a\ne b$, put $h=c_{ab}(u,v)c_{ab}(u,w)$. Consecutive application gives $L(f)=h\,stE_1(f)$ and $M(f)=E_2(h\,stf)$. The polynomial $h$ is symmetric in $v,w$, including the backward case $h=(v-u)(w-u)$, so the product rule $E_2(hg)=E_2(h)g+t(h)E_2(g)$ gives $M(f)=hE_2stf$. Finally $E_2st=stE_1$: both sides equal $(\rho-st)/(v-w)$, with the denominator transformed when the permutation lies to its left. Thus $L=M$. [step 5.1, step 3.1, algebra]

7.1 Exactly the last two equal. On $(a,b,b)$, $a\ne b$, put $h=c_{ab}(u,w)c_{ab}(v,w)$. The two words give $L(f)=E_1(h\,tsf)$ and $M(f)=h\,tsE_2(f)$. Here $h$ is symmetric in $u,v$, including $h=(w-u)(w-v)$ when $a=b+1$. The product rule gives $L(f)=hE_1tsf$. The identity $E_1ts=tsE_2=(\rho-ts)/(u-v)$ now yields $L=M$. This explicitly checks the second repeated-neighbor pattern. [step 6.1, step 3.1, algebra]

8.1 Equal outer colors. On $(a,b,a)$, $a\ne b$, full expansion of the single middle divided difference gives $L(f)=c_{ba}(u,v)[c_{ab}(v,w)\rho(f)-c_{ab}(v,u)f]/(u-w)$ and $M(f)=c_{ab}(v,w)[c_{ba}(u,v)\rho(f)-c_{ba}(w,v)f]/(u-w)$. The $\rho(f)$ terms cancel, and step 4.1 gives $(L-M)(f)=[Q_{ab}(w,v)-Q_{ab}(u,v)]f/(u-w)$. Thus the correction is $+1$ for $a\to b$, $-1$ for $a\leftarrow b$, and zero off edges. The displayed expressions have removable denominators because their original numerators come from divided differences; the final quotient is a polynomial. [step 7.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, algebra]

9.1 All three equal. For $\Delta=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$, expand the three factors $E=(\sigma-1)/(\text{dot difference})$ in either order. Moving permutations to the right gives the complete identity $E_1E_2E_1=E_2E_1E_2=(\rho-st-ts+s+t-1)/\Delta$. For example the $\rho$ coefficient is $1/\Delta$, the $st$ and $ts$ coefficients are $-1/\Delta$, the $s,t$ coefficients are $1/\Delta$, and the identity coefficient is $-1/\Delta$. Both sides preserve formal series by their original divided-difference formulas, so this rational equality proves their equality without inverting dots in the algebra. This supplies the all-equal case omitted in the cited source. [step 8.1, step 3.1, algebra]

10.1 Faithfulness for the KLR action. Moving dots to the right using step 4.1, and replacing repeated crossings and braid differences using steps 5.1–9.1, spans the presented KLR algebra by $\psi_w f(y)e(\nu)$ for fixed reduced words $w$. Termination uses crossing length: every quadratic reduction or braid correction has smaller length; reduced words for a permutation are connected by the elementary symmetric-group braid moves. In the rational-function action each $\psi_w$ has leading term a nonzero coefficient times $w$, and all other terms have smaller permutation length. Distinct permutations of variables are linearly independent over the rational-function field: a shortest putative relation, evaluated on $fg$ minus one selected automorphism's value on $g$ times its evaluation on $f$, gives a shorter nonzero relation. Hence these spanning monomials are independent. The same triangular argument over fractions of formal series proves faithfulness of the completed action, whose elements are the finite sum over $w,\nu$ with formal coefficient $f$. [step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1, algebra]

11.1 Why formal extension is legitimate. There are finitely many $w,\nu$, and each basis vector $\psi_we(\nu)$ has a finite crossing degree. Symmetric positive-degree dots form a central ideal with powers cofinal with dot-degree powers in each coefficient algebra by step 1.1. The PBW module just proved is consequently finite free over its right coefficient algebra and completes coefficientwise. Multiplication extends continuously: moving a formal coefficient through a crossing uses a variable permutation or one divided difference, decreasing its order by at most one, so any finite product has a uniform finite order loss. The displayed completed PBW expansion is therefore the actual central completion, rather than an additional relation imposed on $R_\beta$. [step 1.1, step 10.1, algebra]

12.1 The common degenerate Hecke operator. In the fraction algebra set $Z_r=x_r-x_{r+1}$ and $S_r=(1+Z_r^{-1})\sigma_r-Z_r^{-1}$. On an unequal source component the diagonal term is $-z^{-1}f$, while its crossing coefficient on the target component is $1+(b-a+u-v)^{-1}$. On equal colors this operator is $\sigma_r-(1-\sigma_r)/(u-v)$ and preserves formal series. Thus $S_r$ acts on $\mathcal B_\beta$ in every case. All identities in the next two steps are computed in the fraction algebra and then hold for these regular operators. This use of auxiliary fractions does not assert that a dot difference is invertible in the completion or its quotients. [step 11.1, step 1.1, algebra, construct]

13.1 Hecke quadratic and mixed identities. Let $A=Z_r^{-1}$; then $\sigma_r(A)=-A$. Expanding $S_r^2$ gives identity coefficient $(1+A)(1-A)+A^2=1$ and crossing coefficient $(1+A)A-A(1+A)=0$. Thus $S_r^2=1$, including equal colors. In $S_rx_{r+1}-x_rS_r$ the crossing terms cancel and the diagonal term is $A(x_r-x_{r+1})=1$. Disjoint $S_r$ commute, and dots outside the pair commute with $S_r$. These are precisely the quadratic, mixed and far-commuting relations of [F2]. [F2, step 12.1, algebra]

14.1 Complete Hecke braid coefficients. In spectral variables put $Z=x_1-x_2$, $U=x_2-x_3$, $V=Z+U$, $A=Z^{-1}$, $B=U^{-1}$, $C=V^{-1}$. Both products $S_1S_2S_1$ and $S_2S_1S_2$ have coefficients, in permutation order $(1,s,t,st,ts,\rho)$, equal to $(-C-ABC,\ (1+A)BC,\ (1+B)AC,\ -B(1+A)(1+C),\ -A(1+B)(1+C),\ (1+A)(1+B)(1+C))$. To verify the reductions, multiply using $(f\sigma)(g\eta)=f\sigma(g)\sigma\eta$, $s(A)=-A$, $s(B)=C$, $t(B)=-B$, $t(A)=C$, and $AB=C(A+B)$. For example the raw $s$ coefficient in the first word is $A(1+A)(B-C)=(1+A)BC$; its raw identity coefficient is $-(1-A^2)C-A^2B=-C-ABC$. Interchanging $A,B$ and $s,t$ gives the second word's identical six coefficients. [step 13.1, step 12.1, algebra]

15.1 All five reverse braid cases. Step 14.1 is a rational identity in independent spectral variables, before assigning colors. Substitute $(x_1,x_2,x_3)=(a+u,b+v,c+w)$ on each source component and apply the color-permuting operators. It proves the full Hecke braid separately on $(a,b,c)$ with all distinct, $(a,a,b)$, $(a,b,b)$, $(a,b,a)$ and $(a,a,a)$, because each is the restriction of the same six-coefficient identity and every $S_r$ preserves $\mathcal B_\beta$ by step 12.1. Even when a displayed spectral denominator has zero constant, cancellation occurs in the original regular operators, and injectivity into fractions preserves the equality. Thus the all-equal reverse case also has a complete coefficient computation. [step 12.1, step 14.1, algebra]

16.1 Faithfulness for the Hecke action. The mixed relation moves polynomials to the right of $s$-words and the exact symmetric-group relations reduce each word to $s_w$, so $H_n^{\mathrm{dg}}$ is spanned by $s_wf(x)$. In the action of steps 12.1–15.1 its leading permutation coefficient is the product of nonzero rational factors $1+Z^{-1}$ along a reduced word. All lower terms have shorter permutation length. The shortest-relation argument of step 10.1 proves independence and therefore the affine Hecke PBW basis. Completing at the central ideal of step 1.1 gives the finite coefficientwise PBW module $\sum_{w,\nu}s_w k[\![y]\!]e(\nu)$; its operator action remains faithful by the same argument over formal fractions. The coefficients $1+Z^{-1}$ need only be nonzero in that field, not units in the coefficient ring. [F2, step 1.1, step 10.1, step 13.1, step 15.1, algebra]

17.1 Comparing the explicit tables. On an unequal source $(a,b)$, $S_r+p_{ab}$ has only the crossing term. Its target coefficient is $1+\zeta^{-1}$, where $\zeta=b-a+u-v$. Right multiplication by $q_{ab}^{-1}$ substitutes $(v,u)$ on that target. If $a\to b$, $q_{ab}(v,u)=1+\zeta^{-1}$, giving coefficient $1$; if $a\leftarrow b$, $q_{ab}(v,u)=-\zeta^{-1}$ and $\zeta=-1+u-v$, giving coefficient $-(\zeta+1)=v-u$; off edges the quotient is again $1$. On equal colors $S_r=\sigma_r-(1-\sigma_r)/(u-v)$, and $(S_r+1)(1+v-u)^{-1}=(\sigma_r-1)/(u-v)=E_r$ by moving the inverse through $\sigma_r$. Thus $(S_r+p)q^{-1}=\psi_r$ in the faithful action. Equivalently $\psi_rq-p=S_r$. [step 16.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 12.1, algebra]

18.1 Homomorphisms in both directions. Faithfulness in steps 10.1–11.1 and 16.1 transfers the concrete equalities to the completed presented algebras. Step 17.1 identifies the forward images with the operators checked in steps 4.1–9.1, so all KLR relations hold in $\widehat H_\beta^{\mathrm{dg}}$. It identifies the reverse images with the operators checked in steps 13.1–15.1, so all Hecke relations hold in $\widehat R_\beta$. The coefficient-algebra maps identify the central completion topologies: the symmetric ideal vanishing at the spectral multiset and the all-zero dot ideal have cofinal powers on $\mathcal B_\beta$ by step 1.1. Therefore the maps extend continuously to the stated completions. This proves both directions locally rather than importing a cyclic finite-$e$ theorem. [step 1.1, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, step 7.1, step 8.1, step 9.1, step 11.1, step 13.1, step 15.1, step 16.1, step 17.1, construct]

19.1 Inverse composites and uniformity. The coefficient maps fix every $e(\nu)$ and invert $y_r=x_r-\nu_r$ componentwise. The crossing composites are $(\psi_rq-p+p)q^{-1}=\psi_r$ and $((s_r+p)q^{-1})q-p=s_r$, with the same right multiplication order. Hence each composite is the identity on its generators, coefficient series and completion. None of $p,q,c$ depends on the rank, multiset, interval endpoints, level or cyclotomic charge, so enlarging an interval preserves every formula on the old tuples. Nilpotent dots permit finite evaluation of series, and every proved identity survives a quotient. Rank zero has coefficient algebra $k$ and both maps are the identity; empty positive-rank sectors have zero algebra. No assertion about cyclotomic support, based Grothendieck classes or Specht modules is needed for this local comparison. [step 18.1, algebra] ∎

item.title: Generic nondegenerate local inverse tables on integer colors
item.statement:
Work over a field $k$ of characteristic zero, with $q\in k^\times$ of infinite multiplicative order, integer colors, and the arrows $a\to a+1$. On any finite permutation-stable set of color words, complete the dot ring at the zero dots. The completed local affine Hecke presentation at spectral words $(q^{i_1},\ldots,q^{i_d})$ and the completed type-$A_\infty$ KLR presentation have mutually inverse changes of generators below. This is a local statement; it does not assert cyclotomic support, a tower comparison, or a Specht dictionary.

Write $x=q^a(1-u)$, $z=q^b(1-v)$ and set
$$P_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1&a=b,\\(1-q)/(1-x/z)&a\ne b,\end{cases}$$
$$Q_{ab}(u,v)=\begin{cases}1-q+qv-u&a=b,\\-q^a/(x-z)&a=b+1,\\(x-qz)/(x-z)&a\ne b,\ a\ne b+1.\end{cases}$$
These are explicit, invertible, rank-independent power series over $k$; in particular the result applies over $\mathbb C$. Use $y_r=1-q^{-i_r}X_r$ on $e(i)$ and the source convention $\psi_r=-\tau_r$, where $\tau$ is the native crossing. The changes of generators are
$$\psi_re(i)=(T_r+P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))Q_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})^{-1}e(i),$$
$$X_re(i)=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)e(i),\qquad T_re(i)=(\psi_rQ_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1})-P_{i_ri_{r+1}}(y_r,y_{r+1}))e(i).$$
The quadratic polynomial is $K_{aa}=0$, $K_{a,a+1}(u,v)=v-u$, $K_{a+1,a}(u,v)=u-v$, and $K_{ab}=1$ otherwise. Equal-color dot-sliding constants for $\psi$ are $+1$. The braid order is $\psi_1\psi_2\psi_1-\psi_2\psi_1\psi_2$; on $(a,b,a)$ its value is $[K_{ab}(u,v)-K_{ab}(w,v)]/(w-u)$, hence respectively $+1,-1,0$ for forward, backward, nonadjacent colors.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The integer-color local presentations just stated. Their coefficient ring is the direct sum of one formal power-series ring per color word; no finite-$e$ definition or comparison theorem is being instantiated. In the Hecke presentation the spectral idempotents are the projections to these local rings. Multiplication by $X_r$ on its $i$-summand is $q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. The usual affine Hecke relations are $T_r^2=(q-1)T_r+q$, $T_rX_rT_r=qX_{r+1}$, and the braid and distant commutation relations.

## Proof

**Given:** The displayed presentations and the formal series $P,Q$.

1.1 All coefficients are legal. For $a\ne b$, $x-z$ has constant $q^a-q^b\ne0$. In the last case of $Q$, $x-qz$ has nonzero constant because $a\ne b+1$. In the backward case $-q^a/(x-z)$ is a unit. In the equal case $1-q\ne0$. Thus every denominator is a unit and each $Q$ is a unit. The formulas depend only on the adjacent pair, so they make sense in every rank and in every finite color window. [given, algebra]



1.2 Use an explicit polynomial representation. On the $i$-component let dots multiply, and let a permutation simultaneously permute coordinates and colors. With $\partial_r=(s_r-1)/(y_r-y_{r+1})$, define $\psi_r$ on an equal pair to be $\partial_r$; on an unequal source pair $(a,b)$ let its output in the swapped component be $h_{ab}(u,v)s_r$, where $h_{ab}(u,v)=v-u$ if $a=b+1$ and $h_{ab}=1$ otherwise. The equal-color quotient is a power series because the numerator vanishes on $u=v$. Its product rule is $\partial(fg)=\partial(f)g+(sf)\partial(g)$. Consequently $\partial v=u\partial+1$, $v\partial=\partial u+1$, and $\partial^2=0$. On unequal pairs the square is multiplication by $h_{ba}(u,v)h_{ab}(v,u)=K_{ab}(u,v)$. These computations verify all mixed and quadratic relations, including the native sign $\tau=-\psi$. [given, algebra]



2.1 Three distinct colors. In both three-crossing words the coefficient of the longest permutation is the product of the three pair factors, transported to the same coordinates. Each pair is crossed once. The factors commute and $s_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1s_2$, so the two words agree. This argument does not require nonadjacency; some of the factors can be linear. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.2 First two colors equal. For $(a,a,b)$ write $h=h_{ab}$. The left word is $h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2\partial_1$, and the right word is $\partial_2h(u,v)h(u,w)s_1s_2$. The product of factors is invariant under swapping $v,w$, so its $\partial_2$ is zero. Also $\partial_2s_1s_2=s_1s_2\partial_1$ by conjugating the displayed quotient. The words agree. For $(a,b,b)$ the left word is $\partial_1h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1$, and the right word is $h(v,w)h(u,w)s_2s_1\partial_2$. Here the product is invariant under swapping $u,v$, and $\partial_1s_2s_1=s_2s_1\partial_2$. This verifies the third color pattern separately. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.3 Outer colors equal. On $(a,b,a)$ with $a\ne b$, put $h=h_{ab}$ and $g=h_{ba}$. Expanding the one equal-color crossing gives left and right words $\frac{g(u,v)}{u-w}\bigl(h(v,w)s_1s_2s_1-h(v,u)\bigr),\qquad\frac{h(v,w)}{u-w}\bigl(g(u,v)s_2s_1s_2-g(w,v)\bigr).$ Their longest-permutation terms cancel. Their difference is $[K_{ab}(w,v)-K_{ab}(u,v)]/(u-w)$, the stated braid correction. This equals $1$ when $b=a+1$, $-1$ when $a=b+1$, and zero otherwise. Thus the apparent denominator cancels identically. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.4 All three colors equal. Put $D=(u-v)(u-w)(v-w)$. Expanding the quotients and collecting each of the six permutations gives $\partial_1\partial_2\partial_1=\partial_2\partial_1\partial_2=-D^{-1}\sum_{t\in S_3}\operatorname{sgn}(t)t.$ The numerator is alternating and hence divisible by each of the three pair differences, so this is an operator on power series. This explicitly supplies the all-equal case omitted as an exercise in the source. Together with steps 2.1–2.3 it proves all five braid patterns. [step 1.2, algebra]



2.5 Compute the Hecke generators in the same representation. At an output component set $U=X_r$, $V=X_{r+1}$. For unequal colors the swapped input series $Q$ times $h$ is $(qU-V)/(U-V)$: in the backward case $qU-V=q^a(v-u)$, and the swapped input series is $-q^a/(V-U)=q^a/(U-V)$, so multiplying by $h=v-u$ gives exactly the stated coefficient. In every other unequal case this is the last row of $Q$ directly. Also $-P=(1-q)V/(U-V)$. For equal colors, expand $\partial Q-1$; its permutation coefficient is $(1-q+qu-v)/(u-v)$ and its identity coefficient is $-(1-q)(1-v)/(u-v)$. Thus in every case $T_r=A(U,V)s_r+B(U,V),\qquad A(U,V)=\frac{qU-V}{U-V},\quad B(U,V)=\frac{(1-q)V}{U-V}.$ The equal-color poles cancel on power series, as follows already from $T=\partial Q-1$. Distant commutations follow from disjoint variables. [step 2.5, algebra]

The $s_1$ coefficients are $A_{12}(B_{13}B_{21}+B_{12}B_{23})$ and $A_{12}B_{23}B_{13}$; the displayed identity makes them equal. The $s_2$ comparison is its transposed version. The identity coefficients differ by $(B_{12}-B_{23})\bigl(B_{13}(c-B_{12}-B_{23})+B_{12}B_{23}\bigr)=0.$ This uses the quadratic product identity of step 3.1. These are all six permutations, so the braid is proved. It is a rational identity before any color specialization; the equal-color operators preserve power series by step 2.5. [step 2.5, step 3.1, algebra]



5.1 These operator checks imply presentation identities, rather than identities on a possibly nonfaithful module. For Hecke coefficients the relation is $T_rf=(s_rf)T_r+B(X_r,X_{r+1})(f-s_rf)$. It follows first on the Laurent generators from the affine mixed relation, then on products by its product rule, and on formal local coefficients by continuity. At equal colors $f-s_rf$ is divisible by $X_r-X_{r+1}$; at unequal colors that denominator is a unit. This also gives the spectral-idempotent relation by applying the same formula to the local projections. For KLR use its displayed divided-difference product rule. Thus in either presentation coefficients can be moved past crossings. A crossing word reduces to a chosen reduced word for a permutation: delete adjacent repeated simple reflections using the quadratic relation, and change reduced words using commuting and three-term braid moves. For KLR the braid correction has fewer crossings. Induction on crossing length therefore spans the algebra by coefficient multiples of one chosen word per permutation. The elementary adjacent-transposition sorting algorithm supplies the requisite Coxeter reductions. In the rational crossed-product action, each reduced word has a nonzero coefficient of its own permutation; all other terms have shorter permutation length. Distinct permutations are linearly independent over the rational function field: in a minimal nonzero relation of automorphisms, apply it to $fg$ and subtract one automorphism's value on $f$ times its application to $g$; choose a coordinate $f$ moved differently by two permutations to obtain a shorter relation, a contradiction. Color words in different output components are already independent. Hence the spanning words are independent and both actions are faithful. The argument extends to formal coefficients using their fraction fields and the same finite spanning words. [step 1.2, step 2.4, step 4.1, algebra]



6.1 Both directions and both composites. In the faithful KLR action, steps 2.5–4.1 prove the Hecke relations of the displayed inverse generators. In the faithful local Hecke action, solving step 2.5 gives precisely the polynomial crossings of step 1.2, whose relations were proved in steps 1.2 and 2.1–2.4. On idempotents and dots the two composites are the identity by the spectral decomposition and $X_r=q^{i_r}(1-y_r)$. On crossings the composite is $(\psi_rQ-P+P)Q^{-1}=\psi_r$; on Hecke crossings it is $(T_r+P)Q^{-1}Q-P=T_r$. These are ordered products; no coefficient has been commuted past a crossing. This completes the local inverse comparison in both directions. [step 1.1, step 5.1, construct] ∎

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The parameters, presentations, and the following two explicit
conditional inputs.

[A1] [[lem-generic-cyclotomic-type-a-support-is-bounded-by-rank]] supplies the support input: the algebras in rank $d>0$ are finite-dimensional, their dots are
nilpotent, and every surviving color lies in
$B_d=[\min S-d+1,\max S+d-1]\cap\mathbb Z$. Hecke joint spectral
projectors $e_H(\nu)$ exist over $k$, with eigenvalues $\nu_r$ or
$\xi^{\nu_r}$. The full-line KLR rank algebra is unchanged by any finite
interval containing $B_d$. At level zero all positive ranks are zero and
rank zero is $k$.

[A2] There are fixed pairwise formal series $p_{ab},q_{ab},P_{ab},Q_{ab}$
for every $a,b\in\mathbb Z$, independent of rank, multicharge, content and
window; $q_{ab},Q_{ab}$ are units. On every finite integer window, the local
replacements displayed in the Statement satisfy all affine mixed,
quadratic, distant and braid relations in both directions, with the same
KLR convention. This input is supplied locally by
[[lem-integer-color-degenerate-hecke-klr-local-inverse-tables]] and
[[lem-generic-nondegenerate-local-inverse-tables]], including all five equality
patterns of three colors in the same native convention $\psi=-\tau$; the
cited article and a finite-$e$ instantiation do not replace these local proofs. The first direction
uses the actual Hecke joint projectors and dots; the reverse uses the KLR
word idempotents and dots. No cyclotomic relation, inverse composite,
spectral identification or tower assertion is assumed in this input.

## Proof

1.1 Evaluate a formal series in commuting nilpotent dots by its finite Taylor sum. This evaluation is independent of the nilpotence exponent chosen: every larger truncation differs only by zero monomials. A series with nonzero constant term is a unit by a terminating geometric expansion. Thus all replacements in the Statement are defined. By [A1] only finitely many words survive in any rank. The local relation verifications in [A2], applied on those words, give homomorphisms between the affine presentations before checking the first-strand quotient. No cyclic wraparound or reduction of integer colors is used. [A1, A2, algebra]

2.1 On a first color $i$, write the degenerate cyclotomic polynomial as $f(i+y)=y^{\lambda_i}U_i(y)$, where $U_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(i-m_j+y)$. Its constant term is nonzero in characteristic zero. In the other branch $g(\xi^i(1-y))=(-\xi^i)^{\lambda_i}y^{\lambda_i}V_i(y)$, where $V_i(y)=\prod_{m_j\ne i}(\xi^i-\xi^{m_j}-\xi^iy)$. Infinite multiplicative order makes its constant term nonzero. Both auxiliary factors are units after nilpotent evaluation. Thus the Hecke cyclotomic relation on each projector is equivalent to $y_1^{\lambda_i}e(i,\ldots)=0$. If $\lambda_i=0$, the unit polynomial kills the entire projector. This proves the cyclotomic factorization and descent in both directions. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Denote the descended reverse map by $\sigma_d:H_d\to R_d^\lambda$. On $e_R(\nu)R_d^\lambda$, each $\sigma_d(x_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\nu_r$, or $\sigma_d(X_r)$ has sole generalized eigenvalue $\xi^{\nu_r}$. Distinct colors have distinct values, and the orthogonal word idempotents sum to one. The simultaneous primary projector is therefore precisely left multiplication by $e_R(\nu)$. The Hecke polynomial projector maps to this idempotent: its Chinese-remainder polynomial is one modulo the corresponding primary factors and zero modulo all other factors. Hence $\sigma_d(e_H(\nu))=e_R(\nu)$. The forward map already sends $e_R(\nu)$ to $e_H(\nu)$. [A1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Both composites fix the word projectors by step 3.1 and the dots by direct substitution $x_r-\nu_r=y_r$, or $1-\xi^{-\nu_r}X_r=y_r$. On a word, the crossing composite is $(\psi_rq_{ab}-p_{ab}+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$, or $(\psi_rQ_{ab}-P_{ab}+P_{ab})Q_{ab}^{-1}=\psi_r$. Conversely the Hecke composite sends $s_re_H(\nu)$ to $((s_r+p_{ab})q_{ab}^{-1}q_{ab}-p_{ab})e_H(\nu)=s_re_H(\nu)$; the formula with $T,P,Q$ is identical. The polynomial generators are fixed, and the units $X_r^{-1}$ are fixed because inverses are unique. Thus the homomorphisms are inverse on every generator, without commuting a crossing through its series. [step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For ranks through $D>0$ at positive level use the common interval $W_D=[\min S-D,\max S+D]\cap\mathbb Z$. It contains the support through rank $D$ and one unused ghost color beyond each endpoint of $B_D$. A crossing permutes existing colors and never creates one; nevertheless these endpoint colors keep every boundary edge of a surviving color represented by the integer-line convention. For operations reaching rank $D+t$, use $W_{D+t}$, and enlarge further to contain any specified color and its neighbors. All extra word idempotents vanish by [A1]. Since [A2] fixes the same series for each ordered pair in every interval, evaluation on surviving words is unchanged by enlargement. The resulting maps are independent of windows and glue across all finite rank bounds. [A1, A2, step 4.1, construct]

6.1 Let $\iota_H:H_d\to H_{d+1}$ send each existing Hecke generator to the generator with the same index. It is a homomorphism because all rank-$d$ relations, including the first-strand relation, hold in rank $d+1$. Its spectral projector satisfies $\iota_H(e_H(\nu))=\sum_a e_H(\nu,a)$: the first $d$ polynomial generators give a representation of $H_d$ on the rank-$d+1$ regular module, so their primary projector is the sum of exactly these joint projectors. Prefixes violating rank-$d$ support are zero by [A1] applied to this representation. This argument also holds for $d=0$, where the empty projector is one. [A1, given, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Define $\iota_R=\sigma_{d+1}\iota_H\phi_d$. The established inverse maps make this a homomorphism. Steps 3.1 and 6.1 give $\iota_R(e_R(\nu))=\sum_a e_R(\nu,a)$. The unchanged polynomial generators give the usual prefix dots. For $r<d$, the rank-independent pair series in [A2] and cancellation in step 4.1 give $\iota_R(\psi_re_R(\nu))=\sum_a\psi_re_R(\nu,a)$. These are exactly the standard right-appending KLR maps, so the individually constructed isomorphisms commute with the actual tower maps. Injectivity of the tower maps is neither needed nor inferred. [A2, step 4.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Put $\epsilon_i^R=\sum_\nu e_R(\nu,i)$ in rank $d+1$, and define $\epsilon_i^H$ by the analogous spectral sum. Step 3.1 gives $\phi_{d+1}(\epsilon_i^R)=\epsilon_i^H$. Each last-color projector commutes with every prefix generator, since prefix crossings permute only the first $d$ colors and prefix dots preserve all colors. On left modules color restriction is $N\mapsto\epsilon_iN$, with the rank-$d$ action through its prefix map. Color induction is $M\mapsto A_{d+1}\epsilon_i\otimes_{A_d}M$. Step 7.1 identifies both prefix actions, and the algebra isomorphism identifies these induction bimodules on both sides. Explicitly $a\epsilon_i\otimes m\mapsto\phi_{d+1}(a)\epsilon_i\otimes m$ is a balanced bijection, with inverse obtained from $\sigma_{d+1}$. Restriction agrees by the same projector equality. These formulas are natural in module maps. [step 3.1, step 7.1, construct]

9.1 Composing the two comparisons through the same $R_d^\lambda$ proves the claimed degenerate/nondegenerate tower equivalence. Naturality from step 8.1 intertwines repeated induction and restriction, while step 5.1 covers every specified finite rank cut. At level zero use the identity on rank zero and the unique maps between zero algebras in positive rank; the sole map from rank zero to rank one is the map to zero, and all positive-rank functors vanish. Thus all ranks and levels are included. Every conclusion remains conditional on [A1] and [A2]; no local table identity or based theorem has been established by this gluing proof. [A1, step 5.1, step 8.1] ∎

item.title: A generic word-preserving Hecke comparison preserves ordinary Specht classes
item.statement:
Work over $\mathbb C$, assume AC as in the degenerate categorification
suppliers, fix any finite ordered integral multicharge
$\mathbf m=(m_1,\ldots,m_l)$, and let
$\xi\in\mathbb C^\times$ be not a root of unity. Write $H_d$ and $H_{\xi,d}$
for the degenerate and nondegenerate cyclotomic algebras with roots $m_a$ and
$\xi^{m_a}$ respectively. Suppose isomorphisms
$\theta_d:H_d\longrightarrow H_{\xi,d}$ have actually been proved and preserve
all generalized residue-word projectors:
$\theta_d(e(\mathbf i))=e_\xi(\mathbf i)$ for every $\mathbf i\in\mathbb Z^d$.
This is an explicit hypothesis, not a claim that such isomorphisms have been
constructed here.

Let $\lambda$ be any $l$-multipartition of $d$. Let $S_m(\lambda)$ be the
intrinsic degenerate Specht obtained by ordered affine induction of the
ordinary complex Spechts evaluated at $m_a$. Let $S_\xi(\lambda)$ be the ordinary
Murphy cell Specht for roots $\xi^{m_a}$, converted from a right module to a
left module using the generator-fixing presentation anti-involution. Then
$$[\theta_d^*S_\xi(\lambda)]=[S_m(\lambda)]\quad\text{in }G_0(H_d).$$
Thus the transported simple labels $D_\xi(A)$ characterized by
$\theta_d^*D_\xi(A)\cong D_m(A)$ have exactly the same decomposition
multiplicities in these ordinary Spechts for every charged multipartition
label $\lambda=\lambda(B)$ of the source dictionary in its sorted-charge
convention. For an arbitrary charge order the class equality holds as written;
to use the source labels, sort components and their partitions together. This identifies standard
CLASSES, not necessarily modules or cellular-head labels. If the comparison
also intertwines the residue functors, its transported simple/projective
labels are the same ground-component crystal labels. All levels and ranks,
including level zero, and all supported consecutive residue cuts are included.
item.strategy:
## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The algebras, the proved word-preserving isomorphisms in the Statement,
and the existing local suppliers below. We prove the standard-class dictionary
under this explicit hypothesis; construction of the isomorphisms remains
separate.

[F1] The degenerate affine ordered monomials are a basis, and
$x_{r+1}=s_rx_rs_r+s_r$; evaluation at $m$ sends $x_r$ to $m+J_r$
([[def-degenerate-affine-hecke-algebra]]). On an ordinary complex Specht,
$J_r$ has a basis of simultaneous eigenvectors indexed by standard tableaux,
with eigenvalue the node content $j-i$
([[thm-jucys-murphy-joint-spectrum-is-the-set-of-tableau-content-vectors]]).

[F2] The intrinsic degenerate Specht is the ordered affine induction from
these evaluated component Spechts
([[thm-schur-functor-images-of-standard-simple-projective-and-tilting-objects]]).
The nondegenerate Murphy cell Specht has a standard-multitableau basis on
which all $X_r$ are simultaneously triangular, with diagonal
$\xi^{m_a+j-i}$ at the node $(i,j,a)$ carrying $r$
([[lem-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-murphy-jm-action-is-content-triangular]]).
Its cell and right/left conventions are those of
[[def-arbitrary-level-cyclotomic-hecke-murphy-cell-and-schur-modules]].

[F3] The degenerate projective $K_0$ is the standard highest weight lattice,
its ground is rationally cyclic under the lowering operators, and the
operators are residue induction
([[thm-the-degenerate-cyclotomic-hecke-projective-k-zero-is-the-highest-weight-module]]).
The Hom pairing with $G_0$ has dual projective/simple bases
([[thm-split-simple-projective-hom-pairing-has-dual-bases]]).
The arbitrary-consecutive-cut and level-zero extensions are supplied by
[[thm-degenerate-ariki-categorification]].

[F4] AC is inherited only through the supplied degenerate categorical
identifications ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 Define the integer word character of a finite-dimensional module by $\operatorname{ch}M=\sum_{\mathbf i}\dim(e(\mathbf i)M)[\mathbf i]$. Commuting operators have a finite simultaneous generalized eigenspace decomposition. Applying an idempotent is exact, since a short exact sequence decomposes into its image and complementary image sequences. Consequently this character is additive and descends to $G_0$. The same definition on the nondegenerate side uses eigenvalues $\xi^{i_r}$; distinct integers give distinct eigenvalues because $\xi$ is not a root of unity. [given, algebra]

2.1 Character injectivity on the degenerate side. For a word $\mathbf i=(i_1,\ldots,i_d)$ let $P(\mathbf i)=f_{i_d}\cdots f_{i_1}\mathbb C$ be iterated residue induction of the rank-zero projective. Tensor-idempotent induction gives $P(\mathbf i)\cong H_de(\mathbf i)$, so $\operatorname{Hom}(P(\mathbf i),M)\cong e(\mathbf i)M$ by sending a homomorphism to its value at the idempotent. Hence the word coefficient equals the Cartan pairing with $[P(\mathbf i)]$. Sorting charges does not change the defining cyclotomic polynomial or this algebra; apply [F3] to that sorted realization. These projective word classes span $K_0\otimes\mathbb Q$: divided powers are scalar multiples of ordinary powers over $\mathbb Q$, and the highest weight lattice is ground-generated. A class of zero character therefore pairs to zero with every projective cover. The dual bases in [F3] make all its simple coefficients zero. Thus $\operatorname{ch}:G_0(H_d)\to\mathbb Z[\mathbb Z^d]$ is injective. [F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The component word characters. On the evaluated ordinary Specht of component $a$, [F1] gives eigenvalues $m_a+j-i$ on the standard-tableau eigenbasis. Thus each standard tableau contributes its content word once. Repeated words from different components or tableaux retain their multiplicities. Empty components contribute the empty word. No semisimplicity of a higher-level cyclotomic algebra is asserted. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

2.3 The ordinary nondegenerate Specht character. Extend tableau dominance to a total ordering. By [F2] the successive spans in this order are stable under every $X_r$ and have one-dimensional quotients with joint eigenvalues $\xi^{m_a+j-i}$. Exactness of the generalized word projectors therefore gives $\operatorname{ch}S_\xi(\lambda)=\sum_{t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}[\operatorname{res}_m(t)]$. This counts repeated diagonal words with their full multiplicity, even where eigenvalues collide among distinct tableaux. Conversion to left modules fixes every $X_r$, so does not alter this character. [F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The induction character is the shuffle character. Put $d_a=|\lambda^{(a)}|$ and $W_P=S_{d_1}\times\cdots\times S_{d_l}$. The affine PBW basis [F1], also read in reversed order using its generator-fixing anti-involution, gives the affine algebra a free right affine-parabolic basis consisting of minimal coset representatives $w\in S_d/W_P$. Hence its induced module has basis $w\otimes v$, with $v$ a tensor of component eigenvectors. Moving $x_r$ through a reduced expression of $w$, the cross relations give $x_rw=wx_{w^{-1}(r)}+\sum_{\ell(u)<\ell(w)}c_uu$. Each correction deletes at least one crossing and is scalar; reducing $u$ to its minimal coset representative cannot increase its length. The filtration by coset length is therefore polynomial-stable, and its quotient at $w$ has the component eigenword permuted by $w$. Minimal coset representatives are exactly order-preserving shuffles of the component positions. [F1, F2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Each choice of component standard tableaux and an order-preserving shuffle specifies exactly one standard multitableau: place consecutive global labels into the component boxes in the selected local orders. Conversely every standard multitableau recovers its component tableaux by local renumbering and its shuffle from the component of each global label. Thus step 3.1 and additivity of generalized weight dimensions give $\operatorname{ch}S_m(\lambda)=\sum_{t\in\operatorname{Std}(\lambda)}[\operatorname{res}_m(t)]$, with all word multiplicities counted. [step 1.1, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 By hypothesis $\theta_d$ preserves each word projector. Thus pullback preserves its image dimension and the integer word character. Steps 4.1 and 2.3 give identical characters for $\theta_d^*S_\xi(\lambda)$ and $S_m(\lambda)$, and step 2.1 gives equality of their classes. An algebra isomorphism induces an exact equivalence, taking simples to simples and projective covers to their corresponding covers. In the transported simple basis this class equality states $[S_\xi(\lambda):D_\xi(A)]=[S_m(\lambda):D_m(A)]$ for every $A$. It does not require the cell-module head of shape $\lambda$ to be the transported simple with that same shape. [given, step 2.1, step 4.1, step 2.3, algebra]

6.1 Labels and cuts. Use the identical ordered components and node residues $m_a+j-i$ on both sides; the column-label dictionary $B\mapsto\lambda(B)$ is the degenerate supplier's ground-difference multipartition, with no transpose. If charges are reordered, reorder their partitions simultaneously; the tableau-word sum is unchanged by this bijection, and character injectivity identifies the resulting degenerate classes. Under a residue-functor comparison, simple heads along ground crystal paths are preserved by exact equivalence, giving the same charged ground-component labels. For a supported cut the same word projectors select the same summands; apply the established class equality to that central projector. Choose finite cuts containing charges, the block support and any required neighboring operation supports as in [F3]; the calculation uses only those finite words and is unchanged under enlargement. [F3, given, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 At $d=0$ the sole multipartition, tableau, word and Specht are empty and the class equality is the ground-line equality. At $l=0$ the cyclotomic polynomial is $1$, so both positive-rank algebras vanish, while rank zero is $\mathbb C$; there are no other Specht classes. The preceding steps cover every finite positive level, integral multicharge and rank, and step 6.1 covers supported cuts. This completes the conditional standard-class dictionary without claiming the pending comparison itself. [step 5.1, step 6.1, F3, given] ∎
